## Description

The Great Ferns permanent plot lies in the Great Ferns Provincial Park, on a gentle slope with volcano-sedimentary soils in the centre of the island of Grande Terre. The park is managed by the South Province. The plot was set up in September 2025 at about 380 m elevation and resurveyed in September 2026. The forest was logged until the 1970s and has been protected since 2008. It shows signs of disturbance by introduced deer (*Rusa timorensis*).

The most abundant tree species are *Xylopia vieillardii* (Annonaceae), *Diospyros samoensis* (Ebenaceae) and *Calophyllum caledonicum* (Calophyllaceae). The largest tree is an *Agathis moorei* (Araucariaceae) and the tallest is a *Planchonella sphaerocarpa* (Sapotaceae).
